observed_problem: The historical audit has distilled many Human Review defects into prose invariants or quality-check names, but the candidate does not yet provide an explicit Issue-to-Guard ownership map proving which recurring defects are prevented by executable Core/Profile/Publication guards, exact quality attestations, or the existing Publication Preview checklist. expected_behavior: Every material recurring Human Review issue must have one explicit primary prevention/inspection owner. Deterministic recurring defects require executable regression protection; inherently visual/editorial judgments may remain in the existing Publication Preview checklist when appropriate, without creating additional routine Human Gates.
actual_behavior: The invariant/deep-audit corpus documents defects including Issue #9/#40/#49/#50/#54/#55/#78/#95/#122/#139/#140/#153/#166/#172/#191/#271/#272, but there is no single current matrix mapping each family to an implemented guard and distinguishing machine-checkable from intentionally Human visual/editorial review.
production_workaround: Do not approve PR #310. WU-012H must create and validate an Issue-to-Guard matrix and remove redundant/inapplicable checks before final Human review.
improvement_action: Implement WU-012H: create a material Issue-to-Guard matrix with exactly one primary owner per defect family, require deterministic recurrence protection where feasible, retain visual/editorial judgment in the existing Publication Preview instead of adding gates, and audit duplicate/inapplicable validation for removal.
